Routing settings

3% grade = 30 m climb per kilometre.

At 300 m radius, curve speed is about 50 km/h in this model.

Viaducts can replace tall fills. Set 0 to disable. Rivers can be crossed freely.

Favor nearby, well-defined saddles when crossing ridges. 0 disables this preference.

Distance always has a cost. Earthwork is charged by volume. Curves, grades, acceleration, and braking affect the estimated journey time. Oceans and lakes are blocked; no tunnels.

Route colour: green faster · amber slower.

Controls

Globe: drag or use the arrow keys to rotate. Scroll or pinch to zoom. Double-click a location to center it.

Airplane mode starts above the center of the current view. Hold W/S to move forward/backward, A/D to yaw left/right, and Q/E to descend/climb. Combine keys to turn while moving. Release to hover.

Drag to look around in airplane mode. Scroll or use +/− to change height. Escape returns to globe view. Height is measured above the surface; the camera stays above terrain, water, and ice.

Sea level rebuilds drainage. Mountain height changes the vertical scale. Rivers become ice where the mountains turn snowy. Lakes above 3,500 m become flat ice.

Spatial frequency changes feature size. Noise color adjusts persistence. More layers add shorter scales. These regenerate on release; their values are saved with the seed in the URL.

Map distances use the planet radius in Settings. Heights are drawn with vertical exaggeration, shown below the scale bar. Move the pointer over terrain to see its elevation and physical ground slope. The railway profile shows ground in green and track in yellow.

Mesh detail changes triangle density immediately without regenerating the landscape.
